images.title: Rows times columns
images.purpose: Show why 1/b × 1/d is 1 over b × d by counting the rows and columns of a unit square.
images.composition: One unit square centred with labels on two sides and a rule line beneath.
exact_structure: One unit square split into 3 equal columns and 6 equal rows: 18 equal cells.
Exactly 1 cell (top left) filled reddish purple #CC79A7; others white; grid grey #6B7280.
A teal #0072B2 label above the columns: 3 columns. An amber #E69F00 label at the left of the rows: 6 rows.
Beneath, one line of text with the count.
images.takeaway: The number of parts is the product of the denominators, so the product is 1 over that.
images.description: A unit square of 3 columns and 6 rows with one purple cell, equal to 1/18.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video.
images.teaching_notes: Count columns, rows and the one purple cell.

image_decisions.why: A small grid shows the rule without drawing 12 by 18.
